result: {"findings": [{"severity": "warning", "path": "spec.md", "line": 11, "quote": "- The form and its endpoint require a signed-in user, and contacts are created in that user's account.", "claim": "No acceptance criterion tests that an unauthenticated request is rejected or that contacts land in the uploader's account, so the access-control requirement cannot be verified.", "reproduce": "grep -qi 'signed-in\\|unauthenticated\\|signed out' <(sed -n '/## Acceptance/,$p' spec.md)"}, {"severity": "warning", "path": "spec.md", "line": 15, "quote": "- Each import gets a batch id, and the summary offers 'Undo this import', which deletes that batch.", "claim": "The undo behavior, which deletes data, has no acceptance criterion, including that only that batch is deleted and that contacts typed by hand are kept.", "reproduce": "grep -qi 'undo' <(sed -n '/## Acceptance/,$p' spec.md)"}, {"severity": "warning", "path": "spec.md", "line": 28, "quote": "- When a file has 10,001 rows or is over 5 MB, the system shall refuse it and create nothing.", "claim": "Two limits are combined in one criterion and neither has a passing boundary case (exactly 10,000 rows accepted, exactly 5 MB accepted). The refusal message with the reason and limit, and the 'before it is read' behavior, are also untested.", "reproduce": "grep -q '10,000 rows' <(sed -n '/## Acceptance/,$p' spec.md)"}, {"severity": "nit", "path": "spec.md", "line": 16, "quote": "- The form shows progress while the import runs and, on a refusal, the reason and the limit.", "claim": "Progress display and the refusal message content are not testable as written because no acceptance criterion or observable behavior is defined for them.", "reproduce": "grep -qi 'progress' <(sed -n '/## Acceptance/,$p' spec.md)"}]}
